- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 5–10 days ahead.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.4) and price is near 65–70; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5–10% from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7–14 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward correction of 2–5% for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is flat (0.1–0.3) and price is stable, model often predicts minor drift; avoid large directional moves unless sentiment shifts >0.2.
